sections.title: Answering how you are
sections.content: *Jól* ("well") and *rosszul* ("badly") describe how you *are*, not what you *are* — they're a different word family from the adjectives *jó* and *rossz* you may already know. Both slot straight after *vagyok/vagy* with nothing else to change.

*Jól/rosszul* are built from *jó/rossz* with an *-ul/-ül* ending — the regular way Hungarian turns an adjective into an adverb. For now just learn *jól* and *rosszul* as their own words; the pattern behind them can wait for later.
